name: zolve (multi-turn self-judge single agent with retrieval)

system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: We employ the same technique and prompt templates for all of our tasks.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Concatenating the problem description, solution and C++ solution code for each seen problem creates documents that may be retrieved.
env_context_strategy.note: Episodic retrieval over past problems plus semantic retrieval over a textbook; no repository navigation tools.

observation_format.evidence_quote: we only give the models the execution outcomes of the exposed unit test cases

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: the model must provide a code solution that the same model judge (self-judge) judges
tool_call_format.note: Model output is a C++ program which is executed; no tool-calling API described.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: the model must provide a code solution
edit_primitive.note: Each turn regenerates a complete program.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: In case the code fails on the unit tests, the whole process will repeat again until convergence or reach into the specified iteration

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: multi-turn self-judge single-agent LMs with retrieval process

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: a multi-turn self-judge single-agent LMs with retrieval process to increase the reasoning of modern language models

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: We conduct a human research using an interactive tutoring to further investigate how close a model is to resolving a particular task
human_in_loop.note: The default framework (Figure 1) has no human; a separate HAI study configuration (Figure 2) adds human feedback.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: multi-turn self-judge single agent LMs with retrieval

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: the model retrieves related reference documents and using that as episodic knowledge
long_term_memory.note: Corpus of prior problems/solutions retrieved across tasks.

self_verification.evidence_quote: judges and accepts if it enforces correctness and the intended asymptotic efficiency by yielding the predicted results on all unit tests

retry_policy.evidence_quote: the whole process will repeat again until convergence or reach into the specified iteration (we found that i = 2 is ideal for o1

termination_condition.evidence_quote: within the specified bounds and the process will terminate. In case the code fails on the unit tests, the whole process will repeat again until convergence or reach into the specified iteration

cost_controls.note: Paper states 'it does not aim for minimizing costs' but no mechanism described.

timeouts.evidence_quote: time and memory limits confirming solution complexity
timeouts.note: Per-execution time limits from the problem statement enforced on the program run; no run-level timeout reported.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: the solution will execute against the hidden tests to get the final pass/fail results
eval_hooks.note: ICPC benchmark and evaluation ship with the released code and data.

target_domain.evidence_quote: With 254 difficult competitive programming tasks from previous ICPC (including regional, continental, world final, etc.) contests
target_domain.note: Competitive programming code generation; closest value is swe.

open_source.evidence_quote: We open-source our code and data at https://github.com/kraritt/zolve.
open_source.note: License not stated in the paper.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: We require just black-box access to language model generations; no model-internal information, like as likelihoods or gradients, is required.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: We open-source our code and data at https://github.com/kraritt/zolve.
primary_artifact.note: Coded from the paper; repo not inspected.

first_release_date.note: Basis: arXiv v1 date; no tags available.

pinned_version.note: No repo commit available in evidence.
